subject: Choice Specific Variables in the Multinomial Model

messages.author: 8e619d17df27ef21
messages.subject: Choice Specific Variables in the Multinomial Model
parts:
Dear community,

I am new to Stan and still trying to find my around. I hope my question is appropriate for this forum. 

I am trying to run a multinomial logistic regression with choice specific variables. Say I am interested in party choice of the individuals and I would like to include party specific variables. Moreover, I would like to have a single coefficient for these variables. I was wondering if I can implement this in Stan.

Below is how it is implemented in MCMCpack, in case it helps to explain.

post3 <- MCMCmnl(vote ~
                   choicevar(distD66, "sqdist", "D66") +
                   choicevar(distPvdA, "sqdist", "PvdA") +
                   choicevar(distVVD, "sqdist", "VVD") +
                   choicevar(distCDA, "sqdist", "CDA") +
                   relig + class + income + educ + age + urban,
                  baseline="D66", mcmc.method="IndMH", B0=0,
                  verbose=500, mcmc=100000, thin=10, tune=0.5                     
                  data=Nethvote)

Best wishes,
Ugur

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Choice Specific Variables in the Multinomial Model
parts:
Yes, you can do it quite easily and flexibly. I've been
meaing to write a discrete choice example for ages. You just need
to compute the linear predictor and plug it into bernoulli_logit.

I don't know MCMCpack, so I don't know what likelihood
that model corresponds to or what their default priors are.

You won't need to run 100K iterations in Stan!

- Bob
